variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Octave is largely compatible with MATLAB. It supports `#` for comments.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
d = 3.14;         # double
s = single(3.14); # single precision
i = int32(42);    # 32-bit integer
c = 1 + 2i;       # complex
str = "string";   # strings can use double quotes
chr = 'char';     # character array
data_types.notes: Double quotes for strings are fully supported in Octave, allowing C-style escapes like \n.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
# Matrix operations
A * B
A ^ 2

# Element-wise
A .* B
A .^ 2

# Octave supports C-style operators
x += 1;
x *= 2;
x != y; # Equivalent to x ~= y
operators.notes: Unlike MATLAB, Octave supports increment operators `+=`, `-=` and `!=` for not-equal.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Octave allows `endif` to explicitly close an `if` block, though `end` is also supported for MATLAB compatibility.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: Octave supports `endfor` to explicitly close a `for` block. `printf` is available as in C.

while_loop.title: While Loop

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Octave uses `endfunction` block terminator. It allows function definition anywhere in a script.

arrays.title: Arrays & Matrices
arrays.notes: Identical syntax to MATLAB for array construction and indexing.

maps.title: Structs / Hashes
maps.notes: Structs are typically used for key-value pairings in Octave.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Octave provides `lasterror()` and the specific terminator `end_try_catch`.

comments.title: Comments & Headers
comments.code:
# Comment in GNU Octave
# Multi-line comments or docstrings
# are documented here
comments.notes: GNU Octave uses # or language-specific delimiters (% in MATLAB, ! in Fortran) for comments.

numbers.title: Vectors, Matrices & Numbers
numbers.notes: GNU Octave is optimized for vector and matrix calculations with high-precision numerical representations.

booleans.title: Logical Vectors & Booleans
booleans.code:
is_valid = TRUE
flags = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
booleans.notes: GNU Octave provides boolean types with support for element-wise vector logic operations.

type_casting.title: Type Coercion & Casting
type_casting.notes: GNU Octave converts data between numeric, character, factor, and logical representations.

strings.title: Strings & Character Vectors
strings.notes: GNU Octave treats strings as atomic character scalars or vector arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: GNU Octave formats numerical output with sprintf formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Switches
pattern_matching.notes: GNU Octave executes branch logic via switch, ifelse, or conditional filtering.

range.title: Sequences & Indexing
range.notes: GNU Octave indexes matrices and vectors using 1-based indexing and sequence generators.

iterators.title: Vectorized Apply & Iteration
iterators.notes: GNU Octave emphasizes vectorized functional processing (apply, map) over explicit loops.

oop_classes.title: Object Systems & S3/S4
oop_classes.code:
# Object systems in GNU Octave
obj = list(name = "Model", score = 0.95)
class(obj) = "metric"
oop_classes.notes: GNU Octave uses class dispatch systems (S3/S4 in R, multiple dispatch in Julia) for data modeling.

lists.title: DataFrames & Lists
lists.notes: GNU Octave stores heterogeneous columnar records in data frames and lists.

tuples.title: Pairs & Records
tuples.notes: GNU Octave uses named vectors or lightweight structures for data records.

sets.title: Set Operations
sets.notes: GNU Octave provides native mathematical set functions (union, intersect, setdiff).

modules_import.title: Libraries & Packages
modules_import.notes: GNU Octave loads package namespaces using library or import declarations.
